analysis.title: Barrels, Ballots & the ECB
key_insights: Sales desk commentary (Dimitrios Laloudakis, 29-Oct-2026), not a product of UBS Research. Markets and economists expect the ECB to hold policy rates at 2.5% at the decision later that day.
YTD the ECB has hiked twice. Markets price a December move at 21bps.

The Euribor Z7-Z8 spread is at -0.045, retracing after turning positive during the initial bout of OATs stress. Depending on ECB rhetoric, the TTF front month (at $98) and the durability of European growth in FY27, the spread is likely to join SFR and SFI (figure #1).
EURxxx weakness is likely to take a breather, since little is expected from the ECB. EURUSD made new 1-year lows (figure #2), and risk reversal positioning is retracing after exceeding -1 vol.

If EUR stabilizes after the ECB, the desk sees EURCHF and EURGBP as candidates for a rally. EURCHF would reflect a slight unwind of the recent sharp CHF rally. EURGBP screens cheap in the tactical macro model.

US personal income and spending are likely to keep diverging, with average monthly estimates of +57bps and +30bps. The author has been reticent to argue the gap cannot continue, citing the wealth effect from equity gains (figure #4).
The note flags Polymarket odds for a few critical states, with Texas and Ohio at 69% each and Iowa at 45% (figure #5), with the vote a few days away.
Front-month oil trades at $114/bbl. The Z7 and Z8 contracts keep making new YTD highs, at $88/bbl and $80/bbl.
The March-27 contract trades at $103/bbl. Compared with the monthly average of front-month Brent earlier this year, that would be a y/y change of -4%, a tailwind to headline inflation.

Largest daily movers, adjusted for 3-month realized vol: EURSEK -1.1 std dev, rest of G10 FX mostly within +/-0.5 std dev. NZ rates are still rallying, at -1 std dev across the curve. USDTWD is +1 std dev in EMFX.
